newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CHH's NZ mill upgrade to lower production costs.
newsitem.headline: CHH's NZ mill upgrade to lower production costs.

text.p: Carter Holt Harvey Ltd said on Thursday the modernisation of its Kinleith mill would lower its cash costs for pulp and linerboard by about NZ$150 per tonne.
"We will not be the lowest cost producer but we will certainly be within sight of it," CHH's Pulp and Paper Chief Executive George O'Brien told a briefing of analysts and journalists.
Chief Executive John Faraci said CHH had started looking at opportunities for the company's Whakatane mill in terms of improving that mill's market position, and its other mills.

O'Brien, who said earlier that the Kinleith upgrade would mean the loss of about 150 jobs, said the mill would ultimately have a staff of around 700 from about 960 at present, over the next two to three years.
Faraci said the project would provide returns "well over the cost of capital" over its 10-15 year economic lifespan.
Funding for the project would be out of normal cash flows and the investment would be spread over two years.
"It will not result in a significant increase in our borrowings, nor will it impinge on our dividend," he said.
O'Brien said it was clear that something had to be done with Kinleith as it no longer had the scale, cost-efficiency, or market advantages to remain competitive in the long term.
"It is a high cost producer, leaving it exposed during downturns in world wide commodity cycles," he said.
Brokerage Doyle Paterson Brown said the upgrade, which was two years in the planning, was in line with market expectations.
CHH earlier said it would spend NZ$313 million on the upgrade.

The company said this would result in a 30 percent increase in total production to 600,000 tonnes a year. Of that additional production, 80,000 tonnes would be in market pulp and 70,000 tonnes would be in containerboard. Project time is 18 months.
CHH would mothball its No.5 machine, resulting in a workforce reduction of about 150.
The upgrade involves a major rebuild of the No.6 paper machine, the construction of a new 100,000 tonne recycled paper plant and a speed up and enhancement of its No.2 drier.
CHH is just over 50 percent owned by International Paper.
